reductionDefinition: Fengs reduction converts positive integers in SUBSETSUM to items in KNAPSACK

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Subset Sum = <S, T> | S is a set of positive integers and there exists a subset of S, K where the sum of K's elements equals T
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: The problem is to determine whether there exists a sum of elements that totals to the number T.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: S, a set of integers, and T, a target sum
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether some subset of S sums to T
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {(S,T) | S subset int, T is int} Example: ({1,7,12,15},28)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Subset Sum

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Subset Sum

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Draws the numbers as items and the chosen ones as a bar against the target T, and shows the selected solver trying subsets until one adds up to exactly T.

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Subset Sum

reductionTo.formalDefinition: KNAPSACK = {<H, W, V> | H is a set of items (w,v) and there is a subset of items in H whose collective weight is less than or equal to W and whose collective value is equal or greater than V.}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: The 0-1 KNAPSACK decision problem is given a knapsack with a maximum capacity W and target value V and a set of n items x_1, x_2,... x_n with weights w_1,w_2,... w_n and values v_1,v_2,... v_n find the combination of singular items that provide greater than V value while staying under W.
reductionTo.inputDescription: A set of items with weights and values, and a weight capacity W
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether a subset of items exists with weight at most W and value at least V
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Format: {(i, w, v) | i subset int cross int, w is int, v is int} (i is a set of (w1,v1),(w2,v2),... weight/value item pairs) Example: ({(10,60),(20,100),(30,120)},50,220)
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {(weight,value),...} subset i | total weight <= W, total value >= V Example: {(20,100),(30,120)}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This a brute force solver for the 0-1 Knapsack problem

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Knapsack. It checks that that the weight of the chosen items do not exceed the allowed weight and that the value of the items exceed the required value

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Draws the items with their weights and values, and the knapsack's weight against W and value against V, and shows the selected solver choosing the items.

solver.solverDefinition: This a brute force solver for the 0-1 Knapsack problem
